mutations.label: PN1 the time-based trigger is removed, so the artifact is written only on an exact 50-call boundary again -- 295 of the corpus's 300 browser-walk artifacts read exactly 50, an agent at 99 calls is recorded as 50, and an agent under 50 writes nothing at all
PN2 the flush timestamp is never advanced, so every single call writes the file -- this is on the hot path of every tool invocation and the interval exists to stop exactly that

PN3 the COUNT trigger is removed, so a busy agent only writes every 30s and a burst of calls inside one window is lost if the run ends in it. EXPECTED CAUGHT -- the file pins that 50 calls still writes. Control

PN4 a junk duration is recorded as a call, which the function's own rule forbids: 'an unknown duration recorded as 0 understates' OWNERSHIP SPLIT (#1203pn): running all four at both files shows #1202wl's re-aimed test owns the three FLUSH properties (PN1/PN2/PN3) and #1203pn's owns the junk-duration rule (PN4).
